_comment: The out-of-tree libraries libgit2.so and the git2 CLI link (readelf -d crustify/builds/plain/libgit2.so.1.9.0 and crustify/builds/plain/git2: libssl.so.3, libcrypto.so.3, libpcre2-8.so.0, libz.so.1, libc.so.6; the link line's -lrt is glibc's), one entry each, as the dependencies-schema skill describes. resolved is what the plain build's CMake found (crustify/builds/plain/CMakeCache.txt and its configure log; PCRE2's version from pkg-config --modversion libpcre2-8) and the Ubuntu 24.04 package that installed it (dpkg -S). rust_equivalent assesses each candidate crate, by the areas of the library the campaign uses, against the dependencies skill's Adopted crates criteria, each with its evidence: the areas divide the entities the modules' dependency records count from the library (schedule.json's depends_on.external); coverage was read from each crate's API, soundness from its public API and unsafe code (downloaded sources, read, never built; no deterministic scan), advisories from RustSec's advisory-db, maintenance from crates.io, as of 2026-11-11 (planner run 10). recommendation is the plan's route for each library; decision is the user's, null until the user chooses from the recommendations. libc's decision is the user's earlier one, a wrapper for everything (the glibc side campaign the workspace already pins), carried into the current shape: no crate adopted, the remainder the wrapper. Each library's wrapper is crustify-rs/<source>-crustify, OpenSSL's libssl and libcrypto sharing openssl-crustify; on crustify-rs they exist under their earlier names, glibc-bindings (the pinned commit) and the empty openssl-bindings, pcre2-bindings and zlib-bindings, until they are renamed.

ported.notes: Calendar conversion only: Utc/Local from a timestamp (gmtime_r, localtime_r), reading TZ and /etc/localtime with its own tzfile parser. It has no mktime equivalent: it does not normalise out-of-range tm fields (date.c:564 relies on that) and takes no tm_isdst hint (signature.c:172 relies on mktime reading a gmtime result with tm_isdst=0 as standard time). Local::from_local_datetime returns ambiguous or none instead. clock_gettime, gettimeofday, time and difftime are std's (Instant, SystemTime).

soundness.evidence: 10 unsafe blocks, no public unsafe fn. On Linux they are a NonZeroI32::new_unchecked on a checked value (naive/date/mod.rs:1496), from_utf8_unchecked over validated tz names (offset/local/tz_info/timezone.rs:550) and CStr::from_bytes_with_nul_unchecked after locating the NUL (offset/local/tz_data.rs:158). Since 0.4.20 it no longer calls libc localtime_r (lib.rs:457-472).

bindings.notes: Calls glibc itself, so behaviour and errno side effects are glibc's. Covers files: open/fcntl (O_FSYNC on Linux gnu), stat/lstat/fstat with FileStat = libc::stat, fchmodat, mkdir, utimes, futimens, readlink, access, linkat/symlinkat/renameat/unlinkat (for rmdir), fsync, lseek, read/write, pread/pwrite, getcwd and Dir. Covers sockets: socket, connect, send, recv, sockopt KeepAlive/TcpKeepIdle/TcpKeepInterval/TcpKeepCount/SocketError, and poll. Also covers the get*id calls, sysconf, User::from_uid (getpwuid_r), sysinfo load_average, Errno last/set, pthread_sigmask, SigSet and SigSet::wait (sigwait), execve, pipe, dup2, chdir and waitpid. Lacks realpath, getaddrinfo/gai_strerror and inet_pton (std covers these), sigpending and getentropy. fork, signal, sigaction, mmap and munmap are unsafe fns. Errno::desc is nix's own table, so strerror text differs (EAGAIN gives 'Try again'; glibc gives 'Resource temporarily unavailable'). getloadavg goes through sysinfo(2) loads at 1/65536 precision. No stdio, string, ctype, qsort, calendar conversion, pthread mutex/rwlock/cond/key or malloc.
areas: process identity, users and system information

soundness.evidence: 749 unsafe blocks and 59 pub unsafe fns; the operations unsafe by nature are unsafe fns (unistd.rs:278 fork, sys/signal.rs:930 sigaction, :992 signal, sys/mman.rs:427 mmap, :540 munmap). fds are std OwnedFd/BorrowedFd/AsFd, and PollFd<'fd> carries the borrow (poll.rs:18-20). Dir owns a NonNull<DIR> and is Send but not Sync (dir.rs:47,124). Growing buffers pass their capacity and set_len to the returned length (unistd.rs:937-950 getcwd, fcntl.rs:554-631 readlink, unistd.rs:3714-3745 getpwuid_r). Not UB: from_anything tests Errno::last()==ERANGE rather than getpwuid_r's return value (unistd.rs:3740).

maintenance.publisher: the nix-rust organization's nix-maintainers team and one maintainer (carllerche)

qualifies: process identity, users and system information

bindings.license: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT
bindings.notes: Covers files: open, stat/lstat/fstat, chmod, mkdir, rmdir, unlink, link, symlink, readlink, rename, access, utimensat/futimens, fsync, seek, read/write/pread/pwrite, fcntl_getfl/setfl/getfd/setfd, getcwd, chdir and Dir. Covers sockets: socket_with, connect, send, recv, keepalive/keepidle/keepintvl/keepcnt, socket_error and poll. Also covers the get*id calls, page_size, getrandom, clock_gettime, sysinfo loads, pipe, dup2 and waitpid. Lacks realpath, getaddrinfo, inet_pton, getpwuid_r, sysconf (_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN, _SC_GETPW_R_SIZE_MAX) and an errno setter. fork, execve and signal masks exist only in its unsafe, semver-exempt runtime feature; mmap and munmap are unsafe fns. Its default Linux backend makes raw syscalls and leaves errno untouched, so a ported function whose C callers read errno must set errno some other way (the libc backend, --cfg rustix_use_libc, leaves glibc's errno). It fails the maintenance criterion alone: one crates.io owner publishes it.
areas: process identity, users and system information

soundness.evidence: 1067 unsafe blocks and 70 pub unsafe fns, mostly mm/mmap.rs (9), the runtime module (16) and io_uring; none in the file, socket or id calls used. Every call takes AsFd/BorrowedFd, output buffers go through the sealed Buffer trait (buffer.rs:106-165), and Dir owns an OwnedFd (backend/linux_raw/fs/dir.rs:17-19). The xattr zero-length-buffer UB (RUSTSEC-2026-0486) is fixed in 1.1.6 and outside the used surface.

maintenance.publisher: one crates.io owner (sunfishcode), from the bytecodealliance organization's repository

bindings.notes: Sockets only. Socket::new sets SOCK_CLOEXEC (socket.rs:744-), connect_timeout does a non-blocking connect, poll and SO_ERROR as socket.c does (socket.rs:215, sys/unix.rs:973), and it has set_tcp_keepalive(TcpKeepalive with_time/with_interval/with_retries), take_error, send/recv and set_nonblocking. Lacks getaddrinfo/gai_strerror and inet_pton (std::net covers them) and a general poll: its send/recv timeouts are SO_SNDTIMEO/SO_RCVTIMEO, where socket.c polls on EAGAIN.

soundness.evidence: 215 unsafe blocks and 3 pub unsafe fns (sockaddr.rs:73 view_as, :197 try_init, :232 set_length). Socket wraps an OwnedFd (sys/unix.rs:940); raw fds enter only through unsafe FromRawFd (sys/unix.rs:3057) or the crate-private from_raw fed by syscalls (socket.rs:86). The sockaddr layout cast of RUSTSEC-2020-0079 is fixed since 0.3.16.

maintenance.publisher: the rust-lang organization (repo rust-lang/socket2; owners sfackler, Thomasdezeeuw, rust-lang-owner, github:tokio-rs:socket2)

bindings.notes: Memory maps only: Mmap and MmapMut over a file (MAP_SHARED with write through map_mut, MAP_PRIVATE through map_copy). Every file-backed constructor is an unsafe fn (lib.rs:557, 633, 677, 933, 1453). The only safe ones are map_if_safe, for sealed memfds or fs-verity files only (lib.rs:757), and MmapRaw, which yields a raw pointer. It cannot adopt or release a mapping given as (data, len), so a git_map created or unmapped by C cannot be shared.

soundness.evidence: 72 unsafe blocks and 17 pub unsafe fns. Its safe Deref gives a slice over the mapping it owns (lib.rs:1103, 1698, 1705), with Send/Sync on MmapInner (unix.rs:658-659). The constructors' contract, that the file is not modified or truncated, is left to the caller. The out-of-range advise/flush offsets of RUSTSEC-2026-0186 are fixed in 0.9.11.

areas: process identity, users and system information

ported.notes: covers only the SHA-256 area: Sha256::new/update/finalize replace SHA256_Init/Update/Final with identical output. It is not a C-layout SHA256_CTX: git_hash_sha256_ctx is embedded by value in git_hash_ctx (src/util/hash.h:28-34), which sits inside git_filebuf (src/util/filebuf.h:40) and pack-objects.h:65, so the hash port keeps that layout until its port/layout. Only src/util/hash/openssl.c touches the state.

soundness.evidence: 39 unsafe lines, all SIMD/asm compress backends selected after cpufeatures detection (src/sha256.rs:56-72); x86_sha.rs:48-70 makes unaligned loads within [u8;64]/[u32;8]; soft/unroll.rs:39 reads K32[i] with i<64; block-buffer 0.12.1 (22 unsafe) checks its position invariant before each unchecked set (lib.rs:239-245).

ported.notes: HMAC_CTX_new/reset/free/Init_ex/Update/Final become Hmac<Md5>::new_from_slice (any key length), update and finalize; a re-init is a new value. The digest comes from md-5, so hmac covers its area only with md-5 and md4. The HMAC_CTX* lives in ntlm_client.crypt_ctx (deps/ntlmclient/ntlm.h:72), but only crypt_openssl.c touches it.

soundness.evidence: no unsafe in hmac/src; its digest 0.11.3 dependency forbids unsafe_code.

ported.notes: MD5 only, in EVP_md5's role as hmac's digest parameter.

soundness.evidence: its only unsafe, src/compress/loongarch64_asm.rs:70 (inline asm), is not compiled on x86_64.

ported.notes: MD4 only: the one-shot MD4() becomes Md4::digest.

soundness.evidence: #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in src/lib.rs.

ported.notes: DES_set_key/DES_ecb_encrypt become Des::new and encrypt_block. Like OpenSSL 3.0.13's DES_set_key, which schedules any key whatever its parity or weakness (crypto/des/set_key.c:298-306) and whose result ntlmclient ignores, it ignores parity bits and accepts weak keys (src/des.rs:46-51).

soundness.evidence: des and cipher 0.5.0 forbid unsafe_code; inout 0.2.6 (31 unsafe lines) builds in/out views only from &mut or (&, &mut) pairs of checked equal length (inout_buf.rs:72-80), and its from_raw is unsafe.

ported.notes: RAND_bytes becomes getrandom::fill: the bytes come from the kernel's CSPRNG rather than OpenSSL's DRBG, and a failure is a getrandom::Error rather than ERR_lib_error_string's text.

soundness.evidence: its safe API is fill(&mut [u8]) and fill_uninit(&mut [MaybeUninit<u8>]) (src/lib.rs:87-130); the Linux backend calls libc::getrandom on the exact buffer (backends/getrandom.rs); 114 unsafe lines across the platform backends.

ported.notes: verifies chains and SAN DNS and IP names only: no subject CN for libgit2's CN fallback, no ASN1 string API, and the C caller's X509* (GIT_OPT_ADD_SSL_X509_CERT) only as DER, through i2d_X509; its verification rules differ from X509_verify_cert's.

soundness.evidence: no unsafe in src; no_std.

bindings.notes: Covers X509 (subject_alt_names with dnsname/ipaddress, subject_name().entries_by_nid, X509NameEntryRef::data, to_der), Asn1StringRef::to_string, openssl::sha::Sha256 over SHA256_CTX, PKey::hmac with Signer and MessageDigest::md5, rand_bytes and ErrorStack. MD4 (Md::fetch) and DES-ECB (Cipher::des_ecb) go through EVP, so OpenSSL 3 needs its legacy provider loaded, where the low-level MD4()/DES_* do not. No BIO_meth_* API (SslStream<S: Read + Write> builds its own BIO method), no ASN1_STRING_type accessor, and CRYPTO_malloc/free stay internal; its error Display adds file:line to ERR_error_string_n's format.

soundness.evidence: ssl/bio.rs:107-113: bread makes a &mut [u8] over OpenSSL's read buffer, which OPENSSL_malloc allocates and never zeroes (ssl/record/ssl3_buffer.c:68), and hands it to the user's safe S::read; x509/store.rs:261-273: X509StoreRef::objects is a safe pub fn the crate documents as unsound (deprecated). 1245 unsafe lines; the paths the campaign would use were read.

maintenance.publisher: two maintainers (sfackler, alex), in the rust-openssl organization's repository

ported.notes: ClientConfig/ClientConnection over any Read + Write replace SSL_CTX, SSL and the custom BIO, with SNI, peer_certificates (DER) and TLS 1.2 and later only, which matches libgit2's SSL_OP_NO_* set. Gaps: no OpenSSL cipher-list strings, so GIT_OPT_SET_SSL_CIPHERS cannot be honoured; libgit2 completes the handshake with SSL_VERIFY_NONE, reads SSL_get_verify_result and returns GIT_ECERTIFICATE so that the user's certificate_check callback may override it (src/libgit2/transports/httpclient.c:837), which needs a custom danger::ServerCertVerifier, and verification is webpki's, not OpenSSL's; no CN fallback; verify paths need rustls-native-certs, which loads eagerly rather than through OpenSSL's hashed-directory lookup; the C caller's X509* only as DER; and it needs a crypto provider, aws-lc-rs by default, which bundles AWS-LC.

soundness.evidence: #![forbid(unsafe_code)] (src/lib.rs:332); rustls-webpki and rustls-native-certs have no unsafe; the default aws-lc-rs provider (381 unsafe lines over the bundled AWS-LC) was not read.

bindings.notes: SslContextBuilder covers SSL_CTX_new(TLS_method), set_options (NO_SSLV2/3, NO_TLSV1/1_1, NO_COMPRESSION), set_mode(AUTO_RETRY), set_verify(NONE), set_default_verify_paths, set_cipher_list, load_verify_locations and cert_store_mut().add_cert; Ssl::new, set_hostname (SNI), SslStream's connect, ssl_read, ssl_write and shutdown, ssl::Error::code (SSL_get_error), peer_certificate and verify_result cover the connection. A built SslContext is immutable, while libgit2 changes the live git__ssl_ctx through git_openssl__set_cert_location and git_openssl__add_x509_cert, so a port rebuilds the context on each such option; SSL_set_bio over libgit2's BIO becomes SslStream<S> over a Read + Write adapter of git_stream; OPENSSL_init_ssl is implicit.

soundness.evidence: SslStream<S> reaches bread (ssl/bio.rs:107-113), which hands OpenSSL's unzeroed record buffer (ssl/record/ssl3_buffer.c:68) to the safe S::read as &mut [u8]; X509StoreRef::objects (x509/store.rs:261-273) is a safe API the crate documents as unsound.

maintenance.publisher: two maintainers (sfackler, alex), in the rust-openssl organization's repository

bindings.notes: A platform facade over the openssl crate on Linux: no cipher list, no verify-locations directory, no SSL_VERIFY_NONE-then-report flow (an invalid certificate fails the handshake unless danger_accept_invalid_certs), no verify result codes and no raw handles; add_root_certificate takes DER only.

soundness.evidence: its Linux TlsStream<S> is openssl::ssl::SslStream<S> (src/imp/openssl.rs:431), so it inherits bread's &mut [u8] over uninitialised memory (openssl ssl/bio.rs:107-113); its own 2 unsafe lines are macOS-only.

ported.notes: Not PCRE2's syntax or semantics, though it adds backreferences, lookaround, atomic and possessive groups, conditionals, subroutine calls, \K and \Z over regex-automata, and matches &[u8] through BytesMode::Ascii since 0.20. `$` matches only at the end of the text (parse.rs:375-382), where PCRE2's also matches before a final newline; patterns are Strings, so raw non-UTF-8 pattern bytes (the built-in word patterns of userdiff.h:25,160) must be rewritten as escapes; no PCRE2 verbs or options; its backtrack limit is 1e6 against PCRE2's 1e7 match limit; its error texts differ from pcre2_get_error_message's.

soundness.evidence: no unsafe in the crate's source; its regex-automata dependency's unsafe was not read.

maintenance.publisher: the fancy-regex organization and three maintainers

ported.notes: Another dialect: regex::bytes with unicode(false) and case_insensitive matches bytes with ASCII case folding, as PCRE2 does in non-UTF CASELESS mode, and CaptureLocations covers the ovector and unset groups, but it has no backreferences, lookaround, atomic or possessive groups, \Q..\E, \Z, recursion or verbs; `$` matches only at the end of the text; size limits replace PCRE2's match limits; patterns are &str; its error texts differ. Config regexes, diff drivers' xfuncname and wordregex, and revparse's :/ expose PCRE2's syntax to users.

soundness.evidence: one unsafe site in the crate, src/pattern.rs:30 (a nightly-only Pattern impl); the engine's unsafe, in regex-automata, memchr and aho-corasick, was not read.

bindings.notes: The same engine and options as regexp.c: non-UTF by default (bytes.rs:100), caseless(), NULL contexts; bytes::Regex::is_match and captures_read with CaptureLocations cover pcre2_compile, pcre2_match, the match data and its ovector. Patterns are &str (bytes.rs:124), so raw non-UTF-8 pattern bytes must be escaped as \xHH, which is lossy inside \Q..\E or after a backslash; the bare pcre2_get_error_message text is private (error.rs:92) and Display prefixes it (error.rs:116-125), where regexp.c:90-91 sets the bare message; pcre2-sys vendors PCRE2 10.46 statically when pkg-config fails (build.rs:33).

soundness.evidence: 37 unsafe lines: MatchData::find is pub(crate) unsafe (ffi.rs:409), called with options 0 only (bytes.rs:617,660,707); empty subjects get a valid singleton pointer (ffi.rs:436-441); the ovector slice is built from PCRE2's own pointer and count (ffi.rs:476-490); Code is Send + Sync (ffi.rs:80-81), which PCRE2 allows for compiled code; match data is per thread, from a pool (pool.rs:329); no raw handle is exposed.

ported.notes: Assessed with its default rust_backend, miniz_oxide; its zlib and zlib-ng features make it a binding over libz-sys with the same API, and zlib-rs is another backend. Compress and Decompress cover deflateInit/deflate/deflateReset/deflateEnd and their inflate counterparts (Status Ok/BufError/StreamEnd, total_in/out, reset, message()), and Crc covers crc32. No deflateBound: reftable's block.c:174-198 uses it only to size one buffer for a single Z_FINISH call, which a compress_vec loop until StreamEnd replaces. With the miniz backend a first inflate call with Finish whose output does not fit fails the stream (miniz_oxide inflate/stream.rs:227-250), where zstream.c:106-123 passes Z_FINISH with chunked output, so the port passes FlushDecompress::None (the zlib-rs backend keeps zlib's semantics); Compression::new does not reject levels above 9, which filebuf.c:317-324 turns into an error; an allocation failure aborts rather than returning Z_MEM_ERROR; the miniz backend gives no zlib message text; its output is not byte-identical to zlib 1.3's, which the formats do not require (object ids hash uncompressed data, a pack's name hashes whatever bytes it holds), though tests/libgit2/pack/indexer.c:178 asserts the name of a thin pack libgit2 deflates (unverified across compressors).

soundness.evidence: 37 unsafe lines, 25 of them in ffi/c.rs, compiled for its C backends only; mem.rs:647-656 clamps set_len to the capacity; ffi/mod.rs:9-11 zero-fills uninitialised output before miniz_oxide sees it; no z_stream is exposed; miniz_oxide forbids unsafe_code.

ported.notes: Its safe API covers every use: Deflate/Inflate (new, compress/decompress with NoFlush/Finish, reset, total_in/out, zlib's error_message texts), compress_bound in deflateBound's place and crc32::crc32(start, buf). Deflate::new panics on a bad level or a failed allocation rather than returning Z_STREAM_ERROR/Z_MEM_ERROR (deflate.rs:136-137); its output is not byte-identical to zlib 1.3's.

soundness.evidence: stable.rs sets next_in/next_out from slices, clamps avail to c_uint::MAX and clears the pointers after each call (stable.rs:357-376), and reads msg only as a static C string (stable.rs:92,290); its other ~456 unsafe lines (SIMD, allocator, C API) were not read, and no scan was run.

maintenance.publisher: the Trifecta Tech Foundation, two maintainers

ported.notes: zlib-format deflate and inflate streams with reset and byte counts; no crc32, no deflateBound and no message texts; a first inflate call with Finish whose output does not fit fails the stream (inflate/stream.rs:227-250), so callers use MZFlush::None; its output differs from zlib's.

soundness.evidence: #![forbid(unsafe_code)] (src/lib.rs:25).

ported.notes: CRC-32 only: Hasher::new_with_initial, update and finalize cover crc32(0, NULL, 0) and its incremental use.

soundness.evidence: deny(unsafe_code) (lib.rs:44); its 26 unsafe lines are SIMD specialisations behind runtime feature detection (specialized/pclmulqdq.rs, aarch64.rs).

ported.notes: zlib's C API, deflateBound and crc32 included, reimplemented over zlib-rs, but only as `pub unsafe extern "C" fn`s over a raw z_stream (lib.rs:183,637,1365,1918): no safe API, so no safe binding; it could stand in for the libz the remaining C links.

soundness.evidence: no safe API: every entry point is an unsafe extern "C" fn taking raw z_stream and buffer pointers, so the caller carries every contract, as with C zlib; its zlib-rs core was not scanned.
